sensitivity._note: Tier 4 (Step 17). Varies ONE optional steer against a fixed flawed artifact and grades distribution across concerns, not count. The load-bearing assertion is comparative -- vague must shift the distribution less than single-item -- because an absolute threshold would encode one model's verbosity rather than the skill's steering behaviour. Runs on demand via `run_evals.py --sensitivity`, never in CI.

seeded_flaws._note: One seeded flaw per concern, declared HERE rather than in the artifact. The fixture carries no comments naming its own flaws: only evals/fixtures/<skill>/ is copied into the throwaway repo, so a concern-labelled comment would hand the answer to the reviewing agent and bias the distribution this tier measures. A concern with nothing to find would make its share structurally zero and the shift metric meaningless, so each one is seeded deliberately.
seeded_flaws.correctness: is_expired returns False for a missing row, so an absent session reads as valid
seeded_flaws.security: find_session interpolates the token straight into the SQL string
seeded_flaws.resilience: RefreshRemote has no timeout and no error handling; a hung endpoint hangs the caller
seeded_flaws.style: RefreshRemote is non-PEP8 named and assembles its URL by hand
seeded_flaws.doubt: the module docstring claims everything is fully validated and safe, which the code contradicts
